## Final Accepted Amendments

### `fr-5-99ac0bab`

In `shrimp_feeding()` (shrimp.rs:165-168), the N/C elemental routing for periphyton uses `periph_consumed_biomass_g` (wet-biomass grams) while the N/C routing for detritus uses `detritus_consumed_route_g` (organic-matter grams). Both function signatures accept their respective input conventions correctly (`algae_nitrogen_mg` takes biomass, `detritus_nitrogen_mg` takes organic mass). However, there is no guard or debug assertion ensuring `periph_consumed_route_g + detritus_consumed_route_g` (the value written to `daily_food_consumed_g`) stays consistent with the sum of `consumed_n_mg + consumed_c_mg` converted back to grams. Add a debug_assert verifying `(consumed_n_mg + consumed_c_mg) / 1000.0` approximately equals `daily_food_consumed_g` so that any future refactor of the mass-conversion helpers cannot silently break the invariant between the organic-matter tracking and the elemental routing.

### `fr-5-dc23910b`

Fix hidden N/C loss in shrimp mortality routing. `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:624-642` multiplies corpse and reserve routing by `death_biomass_to_detritus_fraction` and silently drops the remainder, but there is no explicit export pool/action/budget entry to balance that removed mass. Because live shrimp biomass and reserve are still counted in `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:239-248` and `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:324-344`, any value below `1.0` makes total nitrogen/carbon disappear during mortality. Keep the fraction fixed at `1.0` until an explicit export path exists, or add real export accounting.

### `fr-5-87d2c25b`

Validate `death_biomass_to_detritus_fraction` instead of silently clamping it. The new serialized field is introduced in `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:211-217`, but `crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:198-223` never checks it and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:624-626` coerces out-of-range values into `[0, 1]` at use time. A save can therefore persist `-5.0` or `2.0`, yet runtime behavior becomes `0.0` or `1.0`, so the inspectable state no longer matches the simulation. Add a unit-interval invariant and validation coverage, and remove the runtime clamp.
